name: Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1+
description: An **open-source nano quadcopter** from **Bitcraze** that weighs about **29 g** and fits in the palm of a hand. It is built for **development, research, education and swarming**: a dual-MCU board, an expansion port for add-on **decks**, wireless firmware updates, and a radio that reaches beyond **1 km** line of sight with the Crazyradio PA. The **Crazyflie 2.1+** (2024) replaced the Crazyflie 2.1 (2019) with a better battery and propellers, and costs **$240**.
sourcing: Verified against Bitcraze's store pages for the Crazyflie 2.1 and 2.1+ (store.bitcraze.io), its Crazyflie 2.1 product page and datasheet (bitcraze.io), the platform overview, and the crazyflie-firmware repository on GitHub, as of October 2026. Flagged as uncertain: the 7-minute flight time, 15 g payload and charge time are from the Crazyflie 2.1 datasheet, and Bitcraze publishes no separate figures for the 2.1+; weight is 29 g on the datasheet but 27 g on the store description; the $240 price is the store listing in USD; the hardware licence was not confirmed, only Bitcraze's statement that schematics are available; the page is titled for the 2.1+ because the 2.1 is discontinued, though it was requested as the 2.1; and the photo is a low-resolution third-party image showing a Crazyflie with propeller guards and an expansion deck.

pricing.summary: The Crazyflie 2.1+ costs **$240** at Bitcraze's store and includes the control board, a 250 mAh LiPo battery, five motors (one spare), ten propellers (six spare), motor mounts, a battery holder deck and a micro-USB cable. The original **Crazyflie 2.1** was **$225**; Bitcraze lists it as discontinued and replaced by the 2.1+. The Crazyradio PA dongle, expansion decks and any controller are sold separately. robotindex does not sell this product.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The Crazyflie is the standard small research drone: it is light enough to fly indoors around people and cheap enough to fly in **swarms**. The Crazyflie 2.1 arrived in 2019 and the **2.1+** in 2024, with an upgraded battery and propellers that Bitcraze says improve flight performance by up to 15%. The line has since gained the **Crazyflie 2.1 Brushless** (2025) and the Crazyflie Bolt board for larger builds; all share the expansion-deck system. The firmware is open source under **LGPL-3.0**, with development tools, APIs in several languages and hardware schematics published by Bitcraze, which is why this page carries the **Open Source badge**; the hardware licence itself was not confirmed. The base kit has no propeller guards, camera or controller: the photo shows a unit with third-party guards and an add-on deck.
